#4356. Honkai: Star Rail 3.8 will run for an extra two weeks while Version 4.0 is in the oven

The next Honkai: Star Rail update is upon us, and there's a mix of good - and unusual news.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

This final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 1.6.58 - Latest Additions: Aries Gateguard We’ve ranked each Knight in the game in separate tiers, taking into account a few important factors, such as base rarity, active and passive abilities, and their Auras. Additionally, we’ve also considered the community rankings presented by veterans of the game that reflect the current meta. So, rest assured, you will find your favourite Knight ranked on our Saint Seiya Awakening tier list! Looking for similar turn-based RPGs? Take a look at our FFVII Ever Crisis tier list that ranks all of your favourite characters, and our Tower of God tier list, along with a reroll guide. Having a clear and conscious understanding of all the Knights and their place in the meta is going to be very beneficial for any player. Based on the popular light novel/manga series by Masami Kurumada, Saint Seiya Awakening is a beautiful mobile JRPG featuring strategic turn-based combat. Stunning animations, lucid particle effects, and anime-stylised full HD graphics are just some of the cherries to pick through when praising it. I have personally observed the benefits you can enjoy once you make use of the strongest Knights, be it for PvE or PvP game modes. PICK THE BEST KNIGHTS I have compiled a complete list of all the currently available Knights, placing the strongest in S Tier and the weakest in E Tier. Of course, tier lists are always subjective in nature, but I would suggest you add the S-tier Knights to your rosters right away if you can, to enhance their overall strength.

Keep an eye out for future changes to our Saint Seiya Awakening tier list, particularly after a balance patch or feature-rich update where new Knights are released. The rankings of individual Knights will be revised based on the balance changes. With that said, simply click on the big blue button below to view the complete tier list!

Poseidon Seraphina is a powerful Support Saint equipped with cost-effective single-target control mechanics. As the battle progresses, she supplies a variety of buffs to herself and her allies, hence strengthening the lineup in the late game.

Goddess Sasha is a Support Saint with the ability to boost attributes as well as defence, counterattacks, and battle assistance. She can also revive herself or her allies with cheat death. Pairing her up with Saints who specialise in basic attacks or damage dealers with low survivability will yield surprising results.

Owl Partita is a Saint specialising in damage reflection. She acquires Reflect DMG through her skills to deal damage to the enemies. One of her skills, Fated Duel, can reduce the damage she takes, allowing her to survive longer as well as trigger Guardian Owl and Eyes of Owl. Both of these abilities help her mark her target and deal extra bonus damage to it.

Goddess Athena is a Saint who deals damage via managing her energy. She gains energy to replenish her reserve and reduces her skill costs when allies spend energy. She shines when paired with allies that have costly skills.

Cain is a great Support saint. His ability, Another Dimension, can significantly disrupt the enemy’s attack. Try to boost his defence attributes and HIT Status to maximise his advantages. His ability, Kishikaisei, can also help revive fallen allies, provided certain conditions are met. However, he does have a few negative quirks, and that puts him in the middle of this Saint Seiya Awakening tier list.

Divine Cloth Hyoga has very powerful single-target damage and control effects. When there are other Ice Saints in play, his skill, Ultimate Diamond Dust, will deal additional damage. Additionally, his Ultimate Freezing Coffin ability freezes an enemy for 1 round and adds 2 stacks of Frostbite. It restores the target's HP and grants Invincibility for 1 round if used on an ally.

Divine Cloth Sagittarius Aiolos is a unique Saint who excels at dealing physical damage and supporting Physical Attack Saints. Under the circumstance in which he consistently provides extra moves, immunity, and damage bonus to said allies, Aiolos is able to swiftly eradicate enemies with Arrow of Justice fuelled by high Arrow Power.

Pandora is a healing-type Saint with very powerful heals. When friendly units have their debuffs removed, her passive is capable of healing large amounts of HP. She also has active heals when needed. Pandora is also great at supporting, and she can transform debuffs into buffs which greatly increases her teammate’s abilities.

Virgo Asmita is a Support Saint who can restrict all the enemies with the Treasures of Heavens, collect Sapindus fruits to create Acala Shields, and purify debuffs on his allies. He is capable of handling all sorts of situations, essentially.

Andromeda Shun has Thunder Wave, a very powerful single-target control skill. He does not have a very high speed, forcing users to reserve energy in order for him to use this skill. Further, enemies afflicted with Thunder Wave cannot be purified.

All of the Knights included at the bottom of the Saint Seiya Awakening tier list are quite bad in contrast to others, as they display no real combat prowess. They are of the lowest rarity, possessing very low base stats in the Attack, Defence, and HP departments. On top of that, a majority of these Knights are power creeped. We highly recommend not investing any of your precious resources into these Knights.

#4353. KRÜ Blaze recover from opening map loss to beat Shopify Rebellion Gold and reach final

KRÜ Blaze dropped the first map and then took the next three on Saturday 31 October. The win reverses their upper bracket semi-final defeat to Shopify Rebellion Gold and sends the Argentine-based side into the final of the VCT Game Changers Championship 2026. Shopify Rebellion Gold’s campaign ends with the loss.

The result also cuts against the power rankings. Shopify Rebellion Gold arrived as the 10th-ranked team with a rating of 1782. KRÜ Blaze sit 20th on 1742, although their 63-21 record across 84 rated matches is the stronger of the two.

Shopify Rebellion Gold struck first, taking a 47-minute opening map. KRÜ Blaze levelled on the quickest map of the series, which lasted 37 minutes, and edged ahead with a 50-minute third.

The fourth map was by some distance the longest of the night at 70 minutes. KRÜ Blaze closed it out to settle the best-of-five without needing a decider.

The meeting on 27 October had been far more one-sided. Shopify Rebellion Gold won that upper bracket semi-final 2-0, which pushed KRÜ Blaze into the lower half of the draw. Before that, KRÜ Blaze had opened their playoff run by beating Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper bracket quarter-finals.

Saturday’s victory was KRÜ Blaze’s third successive series win in the lower bracket. Both earlier wins were sweeps. They beat Team Liquid Brazil 2-0 in the quarter-finals, then dispatched MIBR GC by the same score in the semi-finals.

That run means they have won seven of the eight maps played since dropping out of the upper bracket. They also came into the event as winners of the Latin America regional final, where they beat Akave Esports Black 3-1.

#4352. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

#4348. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4347. Girl Wars tier list & reroll guide

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version 1.0.17 - Latest Additions: The Trapped Actress - Nero, Flame Emperor's Heir- Liu Bang, Sorceress of Avalon - Morgan, Achilles- Conquered Valkyrie, Huang Zhong- Chocolate Kitchen Maid, Demon-Eyed Juggernaut - Yagyu Jubei, Invincible Sword- Tsukahara Bokuden, Serve the Mistress - Gilgamesh, Special Private Training Session- Lv Bu, Fairy Queen - Oberon, Blitz Emperor - Caesar

If you are a new player and you want to get a glimpse of the meta game, our Girl Wars tier list will do just that. Find out who the best girls to include in your team are, which ones you shouldn't really bother with, and how to reroll to get the most favourable start.  Girl Wars Tier List: How do we rank the girls? The game has been available in Asia for quite some time now, so we do have a good amount of data available. That said, the girls don't have exactly the same stats, so their ranking evaluation is going to be different.

Currently, there are not many UR girls available, but you should expect this to change soon, as many will be released in the future. And, with future releases, our Girl Wars tier list will obviously change accordingly.

About Tomoe Gozen Tomoe Gozen, with her special abilities, such as damage immunity, powerful counterattacks, and a game-changing ultimate, is an extremely effective girl in PvP (but not just there). She is a well-rounded character who excels in both stats and mechanics. You'll notice that she's a staple in many teams. About Christian Christian is a top-tier support character in Girl Wars, as she excels at controlling her opponents and countering fast-paced playstyles. She has the ability to freeze enemies, which makes her a staple force in PVP.

Here's the thing with SSR girls in Girl Wars. For the most part, they've been outdated by the UR ones. That's power creep for you. In many cases, it's better to use SR girls, especially if you are an F2P player, but more about that on the next page.

Even though it's inefficient to max out SSR girls early on because you don't have many food resources, some of them are still very good and worth the investment. About Siegfried The good thing about Siegfried is that you can get her fragments quite easily. So, for F2P players, she's a good, solid option. Her skill, Spear Thrust, is a powerful attack that deals high damage, drains the target's energy and defence, and boosts block rate. It also has a chance to restore a protective Dragon Blood Mark that makes her immune to normal and skill attacks. About Joan of Arc Arguably the best SSR, Joan of Arc, has both abilities, which are attacks that damage a row of enemies, prioritising those with the Imprisonment status. If the front row target has Imprisonment, it spreads it to the back row enemies. Imprisonment prevents the target from moving and reduces healing.

Some of the best SSRs are Frederick, Diao Chan, Guan Yu (She's a great option as a leader), and Oda Nobunaga.

About Satutobi Sasuke Satutobi Sasuke is a valuable support who can be effective once you upgrade her to seven stars. She provides a 10% attack boost to the entire team and her ultimate significantly increases the critical hit rate and damage for her team.

It is recommended to place her in either position 1 or 3 while using Nene as a substitute in one of these positions for additional synergy. Make sure Sasuke's equipment is the best you can get for her. About Nene Even though I wouldn't suggest investing much in Nene, getting her for free to 7 stars is worth it. #4346. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4345. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

#4344. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Review: Everything Switch Sports Should Have Been

Wuhu Island is back, and so is the magic. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort finally recaptures the charm that made me fall for this series years ago.

Say Nintendo Switch Sports Resort three times in a row. Go on, I’ll wait. It’s a tongue twister of a title, and I tripped over it every single time, which is at complete odds with the smoothness the game delivered.

The Nintendo DS didn’t just have great games, it had ideas that stuck around way longer than anyone expected.

I have played every entry in this series. When the Wii turned waving a remote around the living room into a whole new way of playing, I was right there, and I’ve had a soft spot for motion controls ever since. I do enjoy a good sports game, but if I’m honest, it’s mostly Nintendo’s that get me off the sofa. That’s also why I always worry a little whenever a new one is announced, because Nintendo Switch Sports never quite managed to feel like the series I fell in love with.

DualShockers was given a code for this review, and I’ve spent multiple hours on Wuhu Island so far, mostly in single player, on a docked Switch 2. I am nowhere near 100%, and I suspect that could take hundreds of hours depending on how good you are. But the hours I have put in have been more than enough to know this is the game I wanted Switch Sports to be.

The first thing I noticed was how little I was waiting. Load times are much shorter than in Nintendo Switch Sports, menus snap into place, and you can even rearrange the layout of the sports to suit you. Everything feels smoother, less clunky and quicker to get going. After the last entry, that alone felt like a small miracle.

Nintendo games always feel good, and I went in with high expectations of polish. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort met every single one of them. It ran perfectly on my docked Switch 2, and I didn’t run into a single bug or crash in my time playing this. Why can’t every game feel this polished?

My first birdie in Golf and my first strike in Bowling both made me grin like an idiot. It turns out the muscle memory I built up over years of these games is fully transferable, and it all just feels a bit more refined now. Bowling and Golf are still my favourites, Table Tennis gives you lovely control over every return, and Archery is so satisfying that I kept going back for “just one more” target. Tennis now comes with three courts to choose from, which is nice, if hardly a revolution.

Not everything landed quite as well. Boxing was the one I enjoyed least, because the Joy-Con 2 occasionally lost track of me once I mixed in ducks, hooks and jabs. Volleyball, unfortunately, still feels very sluggish, and that carries over into online play, too. It’s my single biggest deduction, and it’s a shame, because Volleyball also gave me one of my favourite moments.

Picture this: deuce after deuce, a match that seemingly will not end, my arms burning. By the time it was over, I was panting and had to sit down and rethink a few of my life choices. Nintendo, if you’re reading this, I desperately need a new Ring Fit Adventure, because that game actually kept me fit.

Then there’s Thumb Wrestling. It’s such an odd addition, and it makes me laugh every time, because it is so very Nintendo. It’s simple to pick up, there’s more strategy to it than you’d ever expect, and I can already see it causing chaos at parties. And yet.

I cannot believe they included Thumb Wrestling over my beloved Baseball. I’d have taken Disc Golf from the original Wii Sports Resort, too. Some of the racket and net sports also start to blur together after a while, so a little more variety would have gone a long way.

My favourite part of Resort is the trio of Leisure Sports, which have nothing to do with winning and everything to do with simply enjoying the island. Power Cruising puts you on a jet ski, with a Joy-Con held sideways like handlebars, twisting to accelerate and leaning to steer. Prop Plane turns your controller into a little aeroplane in your hand, and Skateboarding uses mouse mode, so you swipe across the table to push off and flick upwards for tricks. Luckily, the Nintendo Switch 2’s Welcome Tour trained me for exactly that moment. Generally, these sports are the most creative controls in the whole game, and they’re where I spent a lot of my down time.

Each of them comes with a Sightseeing Tour, where you have five minutes to explore and collect as much as you can. I’ll admit the timer sometimes had me wishing for more. There is a Free Roam mode without one, but none of the collectibles appear there, so it’s more of a scenic drive than a treasure hunt.

There’s no story in Resort, not really, but the sightseeing is the closest it gets. Finding photo spots and cruising past corners of Wuhu Island I’d never seen before taught me more about the place than any previous entry. It’s also the perfect palate cleanser after a sweaty round of Volleyball.

Hyrule has never looked better as they look in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and critics seem to agree!

Very quickly I discovered probably the number one reason that will keep me playing for months: everything counts now. In Nintendo Switch Sports, you could only earn the points needed to unlock new outfits and accessories by playing online. In Switch Sports Resort, every game you finish earns you points, single player included, and you spend them in a shop that rotates its collections weekly and monthly. You don’t even need a Nintendo Switch Online Membership anymore!

What you can pull from the shop is random and different for every user. It covers clothes, accessories, name tag options and sporting gear. On top of that, each sport has its own achievements, which you can unlock solo or with friends. As a bit of an achievement collector, that’s dangerous news for my free time.

For anyone who wants more of a challenge, Island Crown sets you up against increasingly skilled CPU players in each sport, with an Island Champ waiting at the top. The first few opponents are almost charmingly bad, but the tougher ones are genuinely tough. Nintendo has also added a little more “canon” this time, with each sport’s champion getting a bit of backstory. I haven’t beaten a single Champ yet, but I’m working on it.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it. The soundtrack is upbeat and light-hearted, and returning players will recognise plenty of the sound cues. My favourite detail? In Golf, you can hear the waves crashing against the shore and birds chirping between your shots.

The island itself never feels empty. Miis stroll around in the background, and even the CPU opponents use the little stickers that are the game’s only way of communicating. You can play as the newer-style characters and the classic Miis, which made me happier than I’d like to admit. Every session left me feeling a little brighter, which is exactly what I want from this series.

Accessibility has taken a step forward, too. You can choose your dominant hand for every sport, turn on a colourblind mode, and switch off the emote pop-ups from other players and CPUs if you find them distracting. Golf has assistance options, and the tutorials are clear and helpful. You are still tied to the Joy-Cons and motion controls, though: there are no alternative control schemes, and nothing can be remapped.

This is a game for literally everyone. If you just want some fun, need something to play with your family or friends, or want an excuse to move a bit more, this game has you covered. You can play with one to four people locally, go online, take on CPU opponents, and even team up with a CPU partner in some sports. I can already see it becoming the focal point of many a games night.

What surprised me most is how good it is on your own. It’s the most fun I’ve had in a while, even playing completely alone. Games like this usually lose steam once the novelty wears off, but there’s so much variety here that I’m nowhere near running out of things to do.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it.

Online play does have a couple of bumps in typical Nintendo fashion. Bowling has some strange waits between turns, and switching sports kicks you back to the lobby. These are pretty small complaints, though, when everything around them is this good. If anything, Nintendo has undersold this one: for how much better it is than its predecessor, it deserved a much bigger marketing push.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great revival for a series I’m always a little worried about. Nintendo is one of the only AAA players left that still brings real whimsy to the table, and Resort feels fresh, special, and complete from day one. If you want a sports game with actual substance, rather than a handful of minigames, this is the one. If you’d rather sink into a big story, look elsewhere – and if you hate fun? Honestly, I’m not sure how you ended up reading a review about Wii Sports' cheerful grandchild, but I admire the commitment. Somewhere on Wuhu Island, an Island Champ is waiting for me. I might not be ready yet. But I want to become the Island Legend, so I will keep training.

#4341. Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

There's a new Arc Raiders patch that's fairly small, but one with fixes everyone is going to appreciate.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4338. TYLOO’s Lisbon forfeit dents Singapore Major hopes as 100 Thieves edge out fnatic

TYLOO's withdrawal from a HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final in Lisbon has left their PGL Major Singapore invite in doubt on cutoff day. In Europe, fnatic are shut out of the last CS2 Major of 2026 after the final weekend's results went against them.

One walkover in Lisbon looks set to decide Asia’s line-up for the PGL Major Singapore.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. 100 Thieves beat Wildcard 2-0 in Sunday’s FiRe Last Chance final, and the European VRS now places them 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

#4337. The Duskbloods Delayed To 2027 So FromSoftware Can Adjust 'Game Rules And Balancing'

While the 2025 reveal of the Switch 2 came with many surprises, none were as unexpected as The Duskbloods. It's a Switch 2 exclusive, multiplayer-only title from FromSoftware, the developer behind games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring; in other words, not your typical Nintendo game. While The Duskbloods was originally scheduled to launch sometime this year, today the developer announced it's pushing the game's launch to 2027.

According to a post on The Duskbloods' X account, the main reason for the delay was balance-related. Here's the full statement:

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support. During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

#4336. Gods & Demons tier list - From best to worst heroes

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 3.0.10

If you're wondering who the best heroes are, our Gods & Demons tier list will surely come in handy. Each of the heroes specialises in something - be it healing, tanking, or dealing damage - and if you want to have a strong team that can take on every stage in the game, this is the place to be.

I've ranked every single hero, so you will have a clear idea of who you should be using on your team.  About Gods & Demons tier list I have to mention that although I've also ranked the Epic and below heroes, most of them are all in the lowest tier. The reasoning for that is that you will not use any of them once you get the Mythic heroes. You will probably still use one Legendary (maybe, maybe not?), but the Epics and below you will use just for the Codex and as fodder.

I recommend upgrading the heroes at the top of this Gods & Demons tier list because those are the strongest at the moment.

Most of the time, you can make any hero work, as long as the team has a decent synergy. However, you will also need to ascend them, so dupes are good. Getting dupes for your Mythic heroes is not that easy, which is why sometimes you will use Legendary heroes (or Epic in worst-case scenarios).

Which are the best heroes in Gods & Demons? There are a handful of heroes who could be considered the overall "best" right now, but in my opinion, you can make most Mythic heroes work. You can try out various comps to make your team shine, and if something doesn't work how you want it to, then go for something different!

The best part is you can reset your heroes - to do that, all you have to do is hit the Rebirth button, and the hero you've upgraded will be reset to level 1.

Now it's time to dive into our Gods & Demons tier list!

Since the game has been removed from both App Store and Play Store, we won't keep updating this tier list anymore.

Blade Sentinel - Orpheus is hands-down the best hero at the moment. He can deal AoE damage, and once he reaches 50% (at first level, then 60% and then 70%), he becomes a powerhouse. He is worth upgrading and using once you get him.

Goddess of Light - Ostara is the best healer you can have right now. She can mitigate damage, heal, buff her allies' ATK and Crit, and even when she dies, she grants additional healing and buffs.

Indestructible Power King - Grox is one of my favourite heroes. He is the best tank in the game, and he can even taunt enemies. He can curse enemies to take additional damage after two turns, and he is incredibly tanky. He can even revive once per battle!

Nature's Wrath - Freni is a magic DPS who deals incredible AoE damage. She can also bleed enemies and apply Silence if they already have bleed, so depending on the team you have, she can have amazing synergy (with other heroes that also apply bleed) if you manage to silence-lock your opponents.

Resurrection Angel - Seraphel is great if you want to revive your fallen allies. She can also heal the team, making her an absolute beast. She is not as good as Goddess of Light - Ostara, but if you don't have Ostara, she is an outstanding pick.

Celestial Maiden - Liana is another great support who can offer heals, buffs, and CC resist to allies, which makes her top-tier for the Arena. She can also dispel debuffs, and if you manage to upgrade her Soaring Dance to level 3, she will also gain DMG Reflection. An absolute beast for the Arena!

Tribe Guardian - Ella can deal AoE true damage to the enemies, which is a pretty good skill, especially for the story mode. I have been using her since she was the first Mythic I pulled, and she is great. With the right team, she could even be S tier or above.

Blade Assassin - Rein is great with the right team. He can trigger additional normal attacks when allies hit the enemy, and he deals increased damage to targets with lower HP.

Sylvan Spirit - Luna is a Legendary hero, but her kit is quite good. She can apply HP Regen to multiple allies, on top of a flat heal, and she can also dispel debuffs. If you don't have any better healers, she will do great early to mid-game.

I strongly advise against using any of the heroes in the B tier for longer than you have to. Even though we have Mythic heroes here, they pale in comparison to any of the heroes ranked in A tier or above.

For instance, Sand Fury - Billy has a powerful shielding ability, but it only provides shields to two allies. He applies with his Enormous Physique a shield to all allies at the start of battle, but it is not that great.

As for Hell's Roar - Grom, he is a DPS and has Lifesteal, but it is not that great. He cannot self-sustain enough in the later stages, so it's best to just pick a better hero.

Do not use any of the heroes from the bottom of this Gods and Demons tier list for your teams. Their main purpose is to be either dismantled or used to ascend your main characters. The ones you will find in this tier are all of the Epic rarity and below, which is of no use for any of the game's content. Once you unlock them in your Codex, that's it. Move on.

We also have a Angel Legion tier list which ranks every girl in the game with a similar theme to this one and a GFL 2 tier list that also features girls. You might be interested in both!

#4335. The Ratchet & Clank Game You Didn’t Know Existed is Shutting Down

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

I’ll admit, I have a tendency to hyperfixate on games and franchises that I care about, occasionally to the detriment of others. Even so, I like to consider myself sufficiently plugged-into this industry, especially when it comes to relatively big-name IPs like the Ratchet & Clank series. You can imagine my distinct confusion, then, when I heard today that Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble was shutting down, to which my response was, “what the heck is Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble?”

Apparently it is, soon to be “was,” a PvP live service shooter available for iOS and Android. The game saw a soft-launch in mid-2025 in limited territories like Canada, France, and parts of Asia, which probably explains why I have literally never heard of it alongside the fact that I don’t often pay much mind to mobile games in general.

In the wake of Destiny 2's upcoming final content update, thousands of of fans have called for Destiny 3 to begin development.

What’s especially interesting about this particular discontinuation, however, is that the game wasn’t even actually finished yet. That soft-launch was as far as the game had ever managed to get, with its planned global launch officially being scrapped and further development ceasing as of the game’s most recent update today, according to its official home page.

As the home page announcement explains, with the newest update pushed out today to mobile storefronts, no further updates for Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble will be released, and on November 21, the game will be pulled from said storefronts entirely.

This is a feature that looks at how live service games are dying as a popular choice in the industry.

For those who are still actively playing the game, you don’t have to stop playing it right away. While new players won’t be able to download the game from the Google Play or Apple App stores anymore following the delisting, anyone who already has the game downloaded will be able to keep playing multiplayer matches until the servers are officially closed in May 2027.

On November 21, the game will be pulled from storefronts entirely.

The game’s “Qwark Pass” seasons will continue running until the server closure, while the game’s “Super Pass” has been made free, with all of its related content now available to earn throughout the remaining seasons. Of course, said content will vanish into the ether once the game goes offline, so whether or not you can be bothered is up to you.

This also goes for any in-app purchases made on things like currency, cosmetics, upgrades, and so forth. If you’re looking to get a refund for any of that, the developers suggest you contact the Apple App Store and Google Play Store’s respective support lines to determine eligibility. Again, absolutely everything is being erased when the servers shutter in May, so whether you want a refund or to keep playing, you’d better act now.

In its final announcement, the developers offered some words of thanks to the players who joined them for the soft-launch process. “On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development,” they wrote.

While not as high-profile as some other historic live-service flops over the years, the discontinuation of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble is another good sign that live-service games are reaching the end of an era. Aside from a very fortunate few that manage to keep attention with consistent updates and player-grabbing content like Fortnite’s One Piece event, the majority end up crashing and burning well before they can take off in earnest.

Sony in particular has been putting the kibosh on live-service games left and right for the last couple of years, mostly following the disastrous launch of Concord, and it seems even its major first-party PlayStation IPs like Ratchet & Clank aren’t safe from the proverbial axe.

Sony Interactive Entertainment executive Hideaki Nishino doubles down on multiplayer investments during a recent Famitsu interview.

#4333. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "

#4332. Demian Saga tier list and a reroll guide

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 1.6.3

Do you want to know who the best heroes are in Demian Saga? Then look no further, because I've written this Demian Saga tier list to give you all the information you need about which heroes to reroll for, and which aren't worth your time.

This lovely Android RPG has quite a lot of heroes, and while a lot of them can become UL, not all of them are as strong as you might think. Below, I've ranked them all, so you know exactly which select few are worth keeping, and when it's time to reroll for an optimal start. Demian Saga Factions First things first - there are a few affinities that, when paired together, can provide some bonus effects to your team. So, ideally, you want to do exactly that. These are the affinities in Demian Saga:

There is also a Neutral affinity, which can pair with each of the others.

Personality Chemistry You can also gain additional effects from the hero's personality, so depending on which personality they have, you can get either Penetrate Physical Defense, Resist Physical Penetration, Penetrade Magical Defense, or Resist Magical Penetration. Sometimes it's best to change up your team a little depending on which enemy you're facing.

To activate some of these effects, you need to pick either 2, 3, 4, or 5 heroes belonging to the same personality. They include:

Of course, considering all of these bonus effects, you can mix and match a few of them depending on which heroes you're using on your team. Ideally, you want to go for a team that has good synergy in terms of skills (first and foremost), and then focus on the bonus effects (this comes second).

Now that we've got this out of the way, let's check out our complete Demian Saga tier list, as well as the reroll guide! SS Tier  |  S Tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier

Grave is one of the best DPS heroes in Demian Saga right now, hence his place on our tier list. He has AoE damage and can also debuff enemies. He's one of the best heroes you can reroll for at the moment.

When it comes to magic damage, Manes is a beast. She not only deals lots of it but also grants a barrier to allies, buffing their Magic DEF. To top it all off, she can debuff enemies, making her a great addition to a magic team.

All of Cynthia's skills are AoE, and she can inflict lots of negative effects on the enemies. You can inflict crowd control effects with her, such as Freeze and Frostbite, which makes her a great addition to many teams.

Gekkou is a great melee Physical attacker who can inflict knockback on enemies. She is also able to buff herself with a stealth effect, making her untargetable by opponents.

With an amazing kit, Slayer is a beast in terms of damage, buffs, and debuffs. She can become invincible, she can knockback enemies, and to top it all off, she can make them vulnerable too.

Princesa is a mix of support-tank-damage dealer, which makes her a pretty good hero. She can buff her evasion after using Radiant Blessing, and with Shield of Justice, she can protect the allies around her.

Bianca is a support who can pull enemies together with her Gravity skill, and reduce the affected enemy's movement speed. She can also remove all the enemy buffs, and reduce their Accuracy, making her a good member of a team with lots of Evasion-focused heroes.

King Arthur can buff his and his allies' Attack Speed, and his skills can unleash a rapid flurry of hits. He is a decent damage dealer, but he is most useful thanks to his Defense Burst skill.

With Serena Claro's kit, you can debuff and free enemies all around. She can deal good AoE damage, which freezes enemies and applies frostbite, and with Ice Shield, she can pretty much keep enemies at bay.

Judas is okay, but sadly not good enough to be higher on our Demian Saga tier list. He can buff his Evasion temporarily, and also his Physical DEF and ATK. Sadly, the ATK won't come in handy too much, since his damage is not that high, regardless.

Elizabeth can buff allies' Accuracy, which is good against enemies with a lot of Evasion. She can also remove buffs from opponents and silence them, dealing decent damage and inflicting more crowd control in the form of knockback and frostbite.

Bibiane Chain can stun enemies, inflict knockdown, and shock them too. She has a lot of negative effects/crowd control in her kit, but her damage is a little lacking unless she's fully maxed out.

All the heroes in this tier are highly underwhelming, so investing in them is not worth it at all. Even though a couple of them are SL rarity, their kit is lacklustre at best - as for the rest, they are either too low rarity (the R ones) or are just going to fall off pretty quickly.

I strongly advise you not to use them in your team, unless you have nothing better at the moment. You shouldn't even have them if you reroll, or at least you should have way better options. If you haven't rerolled yet, check out the next page to learn how to reroll in Demian Saga.

Rerolling in Demian Saga is extremely easy. However, there is not a lot of need for too much rerolling (in my opinion, at least), because you will get one SL-rarity hero by default, and it's one that you can reroll infinitely until you get your desired one. Here is how to reroll in Demian Saga: Step 1 - Play through the tutorial until you get to Chapter 1-9. That's where you unlock the Recruit option.

Step 2 - Do the single Recruit and pick one of the top-tier characters in the game. Here you can reroll or re-do the recruit as many times as you want, until you get your desired hero. Step 3 - Claim all of the rewards in your mailbox. You will get a lot of stuff, including summon tickets and Gems that you can use to pull a few more times. Step 4 - Go summon! If you got the heroes you wanted, then go ahead and bind your account. If you didn't, then proceed to the next step. Step 5 - Tap on Settings -> Account -> Withdraw -> Withdraw (to confirm it). This option will delete your game data, and then all you have to do is start over.

And that wraps up our Demian Saga tier list. We hope you found it helpful! While you're here, check out our Demian Saga codes article so you can snag yourself some free in-game goodies.

#4331. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4328. Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek, X-Men, And Myriad Video Games Actor, Passes Away

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and important character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.

#4327. 8 Best Anime Where Tiny Details Become Major Story Revelations

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

You know, I’ve rewatched certain anime scenes more times than I’d like to admit on YT or just browsing social media, and it's almost never for the big moments. It’s usually for something small: a character’s hand hovering a half-second too long or a line of dialogue that sounded like filler. Then, twenty episodes later, the show unexpectedly turns that one detail into the thing that rewrites almost everything you thought you knew about it.

Watched These Once? These 8 Anime Hit Harder the Second Time Around

It’s like that foreshadowing or missing puzzle piece coming back later that just makes you bewildered for a second or two at the show’s ingenious attention-to-detail, or, well, certain parts of it, to be exact. It made rewatches feel like detective work, and it also makes you appreciate how much patience and planning go into a story that pays off its smallest choices.

So this anime list is for the shows that reward that kind of attention, especially the ones where you can catch the smallest details and understand why they become so prevalent later, during the climax. Naturally, there are lots of spoilers ahead for the discussed anime, so watch out!

It’s funny that I recommended this show to a friend who went into Higurashi expecting a wholesome slice-of-life show, only to regret trusting my recommendation. It's a horror show that takes some characters’ quirks and uses them as pivotal anchors in later episodes.

Take the first arc, for instance: when Keiichi starts scratching his throat, you get the impression that it's a nervous habit. A few arcs later, you realize it’s the first symptom of the Hinamizawa Syndrome, which explains why people who were perfectly friendly suddenly turn on each other.

The twins are another example. See, you know Mion and Shion Sonozaki look nearly identical, and the show plays with that on purpose, but once you know how the identity swap works, you start to doubt every earlier scene where “Mion” seemed slightly off. I can get why some people think this show is straight-up torture, but don’t knock it till you try, am I right?

Let me preface this by saying we don’t argue between Aronofsky’s Black Swan and Satoshi Kon’s Perfect Blue; I love both. This cult-favorite anime movie’s best trick is how it plays with your sense of what’s real. Mima’s decision to quit her pop group CHAM! and become an actress feels like a simple career move, but as you watch, the film shows how every “step forward” she takes strips away a piece of her.

The tiny, uneasy moments, like her flinching at the fax of the Double Bind script or the way her reflection starts reacting a half-beat late, are the film silently telling you that Mima isn’t in control of her own image anymore. And that’s one of the key reasons I adore this movie, even after all these years since I first watched it.

These anime plot twists flipped entire stories on their heads.

On a first watch, Madoka Magica looks like a bright, pastel magical girl series… until you rewatch it and realize it was telling you exactly how it would break your heart from the very first episode. Almost everything in the show, from the unusual designs of the Witch's Labyrinths to the seemingly innocent conversations with Kyubey, carries far more meaning than it initially lets on to you.

I mean, for crying out loud, the show's opening, with its seemingly disconnected imagery and Madoka chasing after a mysterious figure, becomes much more meaningful once you understand what's really happening. Even small character choices carry weight. Mami’s tea parties, her loneliness, and her insistence on keeping up the cheerful senpai act are all easy to read as charm early on in this show.

Now I’ll be very real with you all here; Odd Taxi looks like a quiet slice-of-life show about a walrus cab driver named Hiroshi Odokawa, and it’s hard to say anything about it without spoiling it. He’s a dry, awkward man who talks in deadpan dad jokes and likes listening to a comedy podcast between fares.

Then a missing girl, a yakuza fixer, an idol group, a struggling comedian, and a nurse with a secret all begin orbiting his cab. What looks like a pile of unrelated conversations turns out to be a tightly built puzzle, and almost every piece of it was planted in the very first episodes.

Early on, much of the dialogue feels like filler, with passengers rambling about their lives or Odokawa making small talk, until you later realize this throwaway stuff sets up most of the plot because a casual remark about a missing person, an offhand comment about someone’s job, or even a name dropped once in passing can fill in the main structure of the mystery. The show trusts you to notice, and it rewards you.

Dive into anime with controversial endings with modern shockers like Death Note and classics such as Evangelion.

Everyone knew this was going to be here, and it deserves it even if it's an obvious pick for this list. Death Note is an anime practically built around the idea that the smallest details can make the biggest difference.

What starts as a straightforward cat-and-mouse game between Light and L quickly becomes an elaborate battle of deduction, manipulation, and psychological warfare, where a seemingly insignificant action can expose someone's entire plan.

Whether it's L noticing the peculiarities of Kira's early killings or Light carefully manipulating the Death Note’s rules, the show constantly rewards those who pay attention. It's incredibly satisfying to watch everything click into place, and while the latter half isn’t everyone’s favorite for obvious reasons, the finale is genuinely one of the most memorable endings in the entire anime medium.

I might be biased for including this because Steins;Gate is genuinely one of my favorite anime of all time, and just a few months ago in August, I had the chance to review the Steins;Gate Reboot VN—and the entire thing was just as good as I remembered.

It starts as a quirky science-fiction adventure about a group of eccentric friends experimenting with a microwave, then accidentally stumbles into a conspiracy-theory time-travel adventure that gradually becomes one of the most intricately woven narratives in the medium. I know that sounds like a mouthful, but anyone who’s seen the show will know the series is just like that in terms of writing.

The genius is in how casually the show introduces certain characters, conversations, messages, and seemingly throwaway moments before revealing just how important they are to the bigger picture at the very end, or just when a certain pocket watch strikes 7:35 PM. Sorry, had to do it.

Look, we’re not even going to get into the debate about how the show ended, so this will focus strictly on Attack on Titan’s brilliant foreshadowing, which led to major story revelations and more twists, as my listicle’s title already suggests.

No matter what you think of his directional choices for the last act, Isayama has an incredible knack for planting seemingly insignificant details throughout the story. Things like the truth behind the Walls, the mystery surrounding Eren's basement, and the peculiar behavior of certain Titans initially seem like separate mysteries, but eventually come together in ways that completely change your understanding of the world in later seasons.

Even ordinary moments in both the manga and anime involving characters like Reiner, Bertholdt, and Annie become far more interesting once you pay attention to their behavior or dialogue, since they ultimately foreshadow their twists.

Naoki Urasawa is one of the most legendary manga auteurs with a wide range of back-to-back bangers under his umbrella, but his work in Monster is honestly one of the best things you’ll ever get to see, as long as you’re patient enough.

This slow-burn psychological thriller is the kind of story where an innocent conversation or a character's seemingly insignificant memory can carry far more weight than you initially realize. Even some of the twists thrown in here at times can recontextualize things you've already witnessed in previous episodes, making them feel completely different when you look back at them.

The mystery surrounding Johan, the Kinderheim 511 experiments, and the disturbing picture-book stories are all excellent examples of how Urasawa plants little breadcrumbs throughout the narrative before gradually revealing their significance.

From One Piece's grand treasure to Itachi's tragic illness, these unsolved anime mysteries leave fans guessing.

#4326. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.
