#4325. Dragon Ball Legends best teams and combinations

The best teams in Dragon Ball Legends are interesting, to say the least. Lots of good (Zenkai mostly) cards and lots of reliable combinations to play with. Compared to how the game used to be, where there was a clear-cut team above the rest, nowadays it’s almost the exact opposite.

There are maybe three or four S tier team comps and around five more pretty close to that level. Team X will counter team Y, team Z might counter team X while team Y will counter team Z. In that sense, the current meta is more evenly balanced.

Some of the players will prefer to make their own compositions, but first, they would need to know which characters to pick. We suggest you skip checking the best team compositions and focus on Dragon Ball Legends tier list if that's the case. How to pick the DBZ Legends' best teams? But of course, at the end of the day, we want to rank those teams right? That’s why you are here, for the best teams in Dragon Ball Legends. So how are we going to do that? Well, we’ll take into consideration a couple of things. To start, how ‘flexible’ a team is. Let me give you an example. ‘Team A’ has a plethora of units that players can choose from to use as a core for that comp and still be top tier. Compare that to ‘Team B’ where you absolutely need certain units (maxed out) to be ‘as good’. That’s a reason to put team A higher than team B on our list.

Another reason of course is, how well these comps can perform at the moment. Some are more expensive than others due to them having two or three Zenkai core members that need to be maxed out and so on.

Now, if you are an experienced Dragon Ball Legends player, you already know which team comps are good and you have your own opinion about them. But, for new players and also players who were away from the game for a while, this tier list of best teams in DBL will give you a good idea about the current state of the game.

You don't want to waste your resources trying to put together teams that are not really viable at the moment.

So without any further ado, let's dive right into our Dragon Ball Legends' best teams!

A huge category with many units to choose from as the core of the team. Yellow SP Android #18 is a Z+ tier unit and for a good reason. She’s the main damage dealer of this team and the only core unit. Her kit is borderline broken after she received her Zenkai Awakening. Usually, you want to pair her with the tanky SP Android 16 (Green) or SP Android 21 (Blue) and SP Perfect Cell Revived (Red). But those are not your only options. One of the reasons why we put Android team so high on our list of Dragon Ball Legends' best teams is because of how easy you can build it. SP Android 21 Evil (Purple), SP Android 21 Good (Green), SP Super 17# (Green) are some very reasonable alternative options.

There’s nothing this DBL team is lacking pretty really. On top of that, there are really many comps you can make as the category is quite big with lots of top tier units. SP Majiin Buu (Green) and SP Perfect Form Cell (Revived) are usually the go-to choices. SP Demon King Piccolo (Aged) (Purple) after he gets to transform is just a beast of a unit. SP Piccolo (Yellow), SP Buu Kid (Blue), SP Android 21:Good (Green), SP Android 21 (Blue). Saiyan and Son Family can be a problem when you running Regeneration.

Well, it’s Dragon Ball and we are talking about Saiyans. No surprise there. This category keeps getting updates and it has a really big roster. There are many different fighters to choose from (all Zenkai of course) with the SP Super Saiyan Bardock being the only core member. The only other member that you definitely want to have (on your bench) is EX Raditz (Blue). His health-boosting buffs for this team are just too good to pass on. SP Angry Goku (Blue), SP Super Gogeta (Red), SP Super Saiyan 3 Goku (purple and green) are your other choices. It would be a shame if Saiyans didn't make it to the top teams in DB Legends.

When three of the game's top units are the core of this comp, it’s only natural to put it this high on our list. SP SSJ 2 Youth Gohan (Red), SP SSJ3 Goku (Purple) and SP Angry Goku (Blue) is definitely a formidable trio. The issue is that once you replace one of these units, there’s a notable drop-off. At least when we are talking top-tier teams in DBL. So even though this is another big category with many units, you have limited options. Other viable units would be SP Youth Goku (Yellow), SP Super Kaioken Goku (Green), SP Gohan (Adult). Most important to note, is that this is the best team to counter Android.

Strong comp but little to no diversity as your options here are limited. Obviously, everything on Hybrid Saiyans teams is based around SP SSJ 2 Gohan (Youth) (Red) and SP SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) as the main carries. The other two viable options that you have for this comp would probably be SP Goten Kid (Yellow) or SP Trunks Kid (Green).

Now this is a team with many viable core options. The ‘staple’ of this team is SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) pretty much. You can go with SP Goku Black (Green) and SP SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) as your offensive fighters, along with SP SS God Vegeta (Purple). Another comp would be, SP LL SSJ Gohan (Yellow) along with SP SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) and SP Perfect Form Cell (Revived) Red as your defence. There are many top-tier units that can complement Trunks on this team. You can’t really go wrong here.

SP Android 18 (Yellow) is that strong. This category isn’t as big as others on our list and the issue here is that the comp is pretty much fixed. SP Android 21 Green and Blue are the other two members usually on this DBL team. But outside of that, the options are limited. Evel 21 Android Purple, SP Mai (Green) and EX Kakunsa (Green) taking up the rest of the slots. It’s a very aggressive team comp, focusing on 18’s damage output and oppressive toolkit.

SP Super Gogeta (Red) is still the main unit in this team. SP SS God Vegito (Blue) is still relevant. The problem with this comp is the lack of defence. Adding SP Super 17 (Green) is a solution but on the other hand, his toolkit doesn’t synergize very well with Gogeta and Vegito. This team is somewhat outdated but still relevant in the current DBL teams meta.

SP Vados (Green) is an amazing support overall for this team. The other two members here would be SP Super Saiyan God Super Saiyan Goku (Blue) and SP Super Saiyan God Vegeta (Yellow). Great units overall that make up a very strong lineup. Alternatively, you can probably use SP God of Destruction Beerus (Green), SP Super Saiyan God SS Vegeta (Future) (Purple), SP Champa (Yellow). Of course, ideally, you want to pair the two Zenkais (Goku and Vegeta) with Vax'dos, otherwise, the team drops significantly.

#4324. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4323. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4322. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4321. T3 Arena tier list - Heroes ranked from best to worst

Do you want to know the best heroes in T3 Arena? Then you are in the right place. Today, we will share our T3 Arena tier list with you. In it, we have ranked each available hero from best to worst. About T3 Arena T3 Arena is a fast-paced 3v3 multiplayer shooter, which is available on both iOS and Android.

In T3 Arena, you take part in 3v3 battles, with each lasting three minutes. There are various game modes, such as team deathmatch, where you have to get 20 kills collectively before the other team to score a win. There is also a free-for-all, where the first person to reach 12 kills wins and many more different modes.

T3 Arena has been developed by XD Entertainment, the makers of Flash Party. It's a fantastic shooter, which I am already in love with. There are over 30 heroes available in T3 Arena to choose from before jumping into the action.

When you start playing, you will initially begin with just one hero, but as you progress, accumulate trophies, and unlock rewards, you will get more. Each hero has different weapons, stats, and active, passive and ultimate abilities. So it becomes pretty tough to decide which heroes are the best. But don't worry. This is where our T3 Arena tier list comes to the rescue. T3 Arena tier list We have categorised our T3 Arena tier list into four tiers - S, A, B, and C. Heroes in the S tier are the best options, and you should try to choose them while avoiding heroes in tier C.

In the future, more heroes will be added and balance changes will be made, improving some heroes and vice versa. But don't worry. We will keep updating this post so that this tier list remains accurate.

Iris, Victor and Labula are undoubtedly the strongest heroes available in T3 Arena. You might be shocked to see Iris at rank one, as she is more of a support hero. But trust us, in the right hands, she is unbeatable. Whether it's Crystal Assault or FFA, Iris performs excellently thanks to her abilities. Her active skills can literally be spammed, which will keep healing her and her allies, making it difficult for enemies to take your team down.

Victor, on the other hand, is a perfect pick for anyone who likes to play aggressively. He has a massive HP pool of 5500 and a shield of 3500 at its default level. If you upgrade it, the stats go crazy. Victor performs really well in close-range battles. He also has the ability to stun the enemies for a couple of seconds.

Cristina is an easy hero with simple abilities and controls. She is a perfect hero for anyone who likes to play passively. If you want to take your time, take cover, and pick your battles, she will suit your playstyle. Her active ability allows you to place sticky bombs around the corners to damage enemies when they walk near them. You can put down up to three sticky bombs in the same place, which means most enemy heroes will directly die if they are unfortunate enough to step within their radius. An easy kill for you.

You can also plant these sticky bombs on one side of the map and then take out enemies on the other side. If an enemy tries to approach from an area where sticky bombs are placed, you will know when it explodes as you get a mark on your screen, giving you some potentially useful information.

Cristina's ultimate ability is also insane; it can instantly kill the entire enemy team if they fall within the range of the mines. However, it takes a couple of seconds before the mine explodes, so the timing is crucial.

Skadi is the hero that you unlock when you start playing T3 Arena. She is a decent hero for a beginner, being easy to use and learn. If you are a casual player and use the auto-fire option, then Skadi is a great hero to pick. Her primary weapon, the Kraken heavy pistol, works excellently with this enabled, and her abilities are also easy to use. When playing Skadi, you can make aggressive calls and then get out of fights using your active ability. On top of that, her ultimate can go through walls.

Gloria is somewhat similar to Skadi. Again, she is a great beginner's hero. However, compared to Skadi, she is much more versatile as she has different weapons for long and short-range targets. If you have played many shooters in the past, such as PUBG Mobile or COD Mobile, you will love Gloria, as the mechanics of this hero are somewhat similar.

It would be best to avoid picking up heroes listed in tier C, unless you are going for something fun. Though these heroes can do just fine in some instances, such as Jabali, who is good at close-range fights, overall, these heroes are weak.

Jabali's active ability allows you to create an energy barrier that blocks incoming damage, but T3 Arena is a fast-paced shooter; within a second, three heroes will be attacking you from different directions. It makes no sense to protect bullets from one side. And also, you can't shoot when the energy barrier is in effect. Its ultimate is excellent for taking down enemies that have low HP, but what if you have heroes like Victor in the opponent team? You will hardly cause a dent to his HP.

With this, we come to the end of our T3 Arena tier list. For more tips and guides, stay tuned with us.

#4319. Best planes in Wings of Heroes

It's time to think like a WW2 pilot to dominate the skies - which is where our handy guide to the best planes in Wings of Heroes swoops in to save the day!

Updated on November  7th, 2026 - Version 2.3.3 - Added: Lockheed P-38G Lightning, Messerschmitt Bf 110 G-2, North American A-36 Apache, Reggiane Re.2001 CN, Supermarine Spitfire Mk IIa

Wings of Heroes is a multiplayer game inspired by the Second World War, and since there are lots of planes, you probably won't have the resources to maintain them all. And while it's always tempting to pick a plane based on its looks alone (we've all judged a book by its proverbial cover, haven't we?), it's worth strategising the best stats for each plane to dominate the skies across every tier.

If you're feeling overwhelmed, fret not - I've shared the best planes in Wings of Heroes in each tier.

Of course, I suggest you take it with a grain of salt, because there is no "one plane fits all" answer here. From fighters to bombers, each one comes with different stats, so choosing something that fits your preferred play style will make a difference.

And speaking of WW2, you might fancy grabbing freebies for some interesting war-themed romps on mobile too! Why not have a go at these Last War Survival codes and Era of Warfare gift codes? Types of aircraft in Wings of Heroes:

Both of these are equal in terms of power. They are not ideal, since they are LF aircraft, but at least you get to learn how to manoeuvre the other planes once you have access to them.

For a Tier II plane, this Fighter is incredibly fast and has a relatively short turn time. It deals good DPS, but it has very (VERY) low survivability. I recommend you use it for the agility it has, but pay attention to the enemy shots, because things can get heated pretty fast.

Although this bomber is a slow one, it is a great choice if you want a well-rounded aircraft. It deals good damage, it has good survivability, and it manoeuvres as well as any other Tier III plane. I particularly like the damage potential it has.

This fun little aircraft is swift and deadly. It has fairly low survival rates, but it has speed, and it can turn in as little as 18 seconds. It also deals okay-ish damage, but you need to be careful with the hits. If you get hit a little bit too much, things could get dangerous.

These three aircraft from Tier V are just amazing. If you manage to upgrade them to max rank, they can be bonkers well into the late game. While the Junkers can deal amazing DPS, it has slightly lower turn time, but crazy survivability. You can sit there and tank, while you eliminate pretty much anybody standing in your way.

As for the other two MFs, they have balanced stats, but a really large arsenal. They also have suspended armaments, which can come in handy. They are both balanced, but deadly. I particularly like the PE-2-31.

These two bombers are pretty similar. They are not too slow to deem them unusable, and they are packed full of missiles and weaponry that deal well over 120 DPS. If you like bombers, one of these two is a must-have. I would personally lean more towards the Mitsubishi one.

The BF 110 G-2 is a reliable multirole fighter. It can deal good damage, it can go fast (so you can catch up with the opponents), and it has okay armour. It's got a relatively decent turn time, and the DPS is something else. The best part is, if you manage to land your suspended armament (the missile), you can one-shot pretty much any opponent.

This outstanding Japanese bomber is fitted with enough firepower to take on an entire enemy squad. It has really good armour, the speed is decent, and although the turn time is higher than you would like, it doesn't deem it unusable. The suspended 8 armaments it has deal okay DPS, and when combined with the 5 other weapons, it's a kill machine.

The Spitfire Fighter is one of the fastest ones you can get your hands on. It deals good damage and is the complete opposite of the Flying Fortress. As the name suggests, the latter is an absolute unit, fitted with heavy weaponry and a turn time that rivals that of the Titanic sinking.

The Flying Fortress is SLOW, but it packs a big, flaming punch. As for the Spitfire, it is super fast, and it is all-around a good choice if you want to hound an enemy.

The P-51 Mustang is an outstanding plane that can deal lots of damage no matter the situation. If you manage to unlock it, it's a must-play.

#4316. Death Stranding Isolations Animated Series Gets New Teaser Trailer

A new teaser trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an upcoming animated series coming exclusively to Disney+ and Hulu next year, premiered during Kojima Productions’ 10th Anniversary Exhibition Beyond the Strand. The series was first announced last year.

Death Stranding Isolations tells an original story in the Death Stranding universe set immediately after the events of the first game. Isolations is created by Japanese animation studio E&H Production (Ninja Kamui, Bullet/Bullet, Magic Knight Rayerath) and directed by Takayuki Sano.  Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima serves as executive producer.

Today’s teaser video provides the following story synopsis:

The Death Stranding—a catastrophic series of explosions caused when the dead crept into our world and collided with the living.

In the wake of this cataclysm, many were forced to live in absolute isolation—among them, a young girl. Although this lonely existence was forced upon her, she soon grows to prefer solitude, eschewing all opportunities for real human connection and allowing herself to be strung along by fate.

In Death Stranding, legendary game creator Hideo Kojima brought you a haunting vision of a shattered world. Now, that world expands into new frontiers with a brand-new animation series.

Under the guidance of director Takayuki Sano, world-class hand-drawn animations have been brought to life by renowned studio “E&H production” (NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET, the Magic Knight Rayearth television series).

The story is set in North America immediately after Sam—the protagonist of the game—reconnects the continent by means of the Chiral Network. However, as America is reborn from the ashes, the renewed connections that bind it together bring about new and unforeseen consequences.

In this tumultuous new landscape, there are some who walk a different path to the one chosen by Sam and his Bridges comrades: a wise old man who connects people through a method that defies all reckoning; a female soldier ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction; a boy who seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life...and of course, the girl who chose to sever all ties with the outside world...Fate has other plans for her, however, and chance encounters see her launched headfirst into a world she does not recognize.

Death Stranding Isolations is coming to Disney+ and Hulu in 2027. It’s one of the three planned big-screen adaptations of the series. An animated movie called Death Stranding: Mosquito (working title) is also in the works alongside a live-action Death Stranding film by A24.

For more on Death Stranding, check out our reviews for the first game and its 2025 sequel. You can also read the latest update on Kojima Productions’ upcoming stealth-espionage game, Physint.

#4315. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4314. Metria tier list: Ranking all currently available characters

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 6.3.0 - Added: [Green Hammer Knight] Popodero, [Purple Piercer Knight] Zescole

Asobimo’s Metria has captured our interest recently, and despite a relatively small roster for a game of its type, each of the playable characters featured has its own appeal. But for those more concerned about stats than other attributes, what’s important is knowing where they place and what you should be going for.

While set up like a traditional JRPG, Metria more closely resembles a hack 'n slash. Rather than using a given set of characters in a turn-based setup, you'll be constantly switching between them during quickly moving, flowing battles against a variety of enemies. Spacing and dodging will be your friend, but being able to do damage and make use of your moves is also key to success.

Given that the roster is fairly limited currently, there aren't any downright "bad" characters - we're going to keep the rankings to the S-B tiers. We'll be sure to revisit when more characters are released, especially if Metria manages to find its footing and start making an even bigger splash.

You'll also want to use our reroll guide to Metria as well, but for a brief overview, you should know that each character has an element with which they're in affinity. This boosts their damage against enemies weak to that type and means that they will also take greater damage in certain situations. Characters also have four slots where you can apply upgrades in the form of tarot cards, some of which provide extra boosts to certain characters or those with a certain affinity.

If you take a look at whatever characters you get, you can open the details tab to see all their damage types, stats and more broken down. We also have a guide taking you through the beginning of the game and explaining all the basic mechanics if you want to know more!

That’s where our latest Metria tier list comes in - we’ll be looking at the currently available characters, ranking them based on our experience and their usefulness, and discussing why we’ve made these placements! So let’s get started with…

The top of the Metria tier list is where the best characters, stats and intuitiveness-wise, are placed, starting with the demi-human Aru. One of the indisputably good characters stat-wise, Aru also uses ranged attacks, which makes her one of the few characters to do so. She’s also available from early on and her abilities in this case make a big difference in pushing her into the top tier.

Stats-wise, Rio is nothing to write home about. However, if you’ve ever played a Japanese hack ‘n slash or JRPG, you’ll recognise him as your bog-standard protagonist. Conversely, this means he’s also easy to learn and has a very intuitive move set, so keeping him as the standard centre of your party is an easy recommendation to make.

This tier is where we're placing characters that are easy to learn but perhaps not the ultimate stats-wise. Starting with Lunaria, Begius’ daughter and currently the only magic user in the game, technically speaking. Lunaria’s abilities mix up what has up until now in the game's roster been a fairly consistent style of play between ranged and melee.

Possessing similar debuff abilities to Shash, Zescol is a melee character that offers good stats and the ability to capitalise on debuffs. Since most enemies close the gap quite quickly, she’s a good pick if you want to bring their stats down but not try to keep at a distance as you would with Shash.

It’s often said that Japanese developers are surprised by the popularity of cool old guy characters in their games. Asobimo seems aware of this, as Begius is one of the characters you’ll have from almost near the beginning, and his defensive playstyle makes him good for durability and big hits.

While not bad by any means, characters in B tier are just lacklustre to use at the moment, or simply have better versions in other characters. Dino’s focus on the earth element, for example, isn’t exactly a stand-out given that you’ll likely have access to Begius beforehand, and his move set does it better. However, as you may have noticed, there aren’t really any terrible characters at the moment, but you’ve still got better options.

While Lucas does usually hit a bit higher in some players’ estimations, we found that his move set simply doesn’t measure up to what other characters have available. He’s not a bad pick, stats-wise, of course, but Rio is easier to learn, and other characters have better abilities. He’s nonetheless a solid third pick for your team.

You’ll notice that the character roster essentially doubles when you take into account the SSR versions of characters. Unlike other games, these aren’t just palette swaps, but they entirely switch up a character’s playstyle, including their element. Solid Aqua Shield Begius, for example, switches his element from earth to water, and offers a surprising way to refresh his playstyle.

You can roll these in the gacha, and if you need to know more about currency uses, you can check out our guide to Metria's currency. You'll note that win rates are, naturally, quite low. Fortunately, Metria is one of many gachas now offering pity pulls, offering a guaranteed SSR character after a certain number, which is surprisingly good value with the currently limited roster.

Keep an eye on these, because if you pick one, it may boost - or lower - a character in your estimations. It also offers a reason to play with the gacha system to grab these unique versions of the characters. And since you're a fan of character rankings, you can use our tier list for Battle Cats, and thisInfinite Magicraid tier list. If there are other gachas that you enjoy, take a look around! The chances are we've covered it.

#4311. EA Reportedly Closed BioWare To Invest In Developing Star Wars Battlefront III Instead Of The Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a new Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

There's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

#4310. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4309. Super Auto Pets tier list for November 2026

Are you looking for a Super Auto Pets tier list? Well, you're in luck, since we just made one especially for you. In it, we've ranked the pets from the best to the worst.

For those of you who don't know, Super Auto Pets is a multiplayer strategy (auto chess) game that was released on the 24th of September 2021 by Team Wood Games. This free-to-play game is available on iOS, Android, Steam, and even browsers. The synopsis is simple as can be - you pick a pet with which to fight shoulder-to-shoulder against other players.

SUPER AUTO PETS TIER LIST It's time to talk about pets in detail! At the time of writing this article, there are 166 pets available, which are divided into different sub-categories. Some can be obtained through the shop, and some in exclusive packs. Each pet has a special ability that works well when paired with others. For such mechanics to work to your advantage, a good strategy is needed, as well as an understanding of which character will be profitable and powerful. That is why this Super Auto Pets tier list of the best pets was created - it will make everything less complicated for you!

Pets that are at the top of our Super Auto Pets tier list are the ones that you should build your team around. They are the meta-characters right now, and you need to level them up as fast as possible because of the value they bring to your squad.

You definitely won't go wrong by using the A-tier characters because they are all quite good, but you also have to take into account their abilities. They may require a small amount of additional investment to be as effective as the options in the higher tier.

The majority of pets that fall within the B-tier are quite average. They are not outstanding, but they can come in handy when facing certain foes and in certain teams. While they're still acceptable, there's a limit to how much you can rely on them.

C-tier pets aren't worth investing in, but if there are no other options, these pets will also do - at least, initially. Some of them that have synergies with others can turn out quite useful (like Camel), but only if they are a part of a certain team.

When it comes to pets on this tier, it is worth mentioning that they lose out on many points to the pets on the tier list above, but they are still playable.

It's better not to consider these pets for investment during a battle, as they bring very few buffs and will do nothing but take up a slot in the team. Some of them, like Beetle, can be useful in the first round, but other than that, just avoid them. They are at the bottom of the Super Auto Pets tier list for a reason.

Our Super Auto Pets tier list was created to make the game easier to tackle, but it's in no way intended to discourage you from playing whatever you prefer. If you have personal preferences, then feel free to go with those. Just remember, the game will likely pose a greater challenge than it needs to! But maybe that's how you prefer it! We hope this guide was helpful for you - and while you are here, take a look at our list of the best strategy games for Android.

#4308. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4307. Hero Tale best builds - One for melee, one for ranged characters

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 1.4.18

There are a million builds in Hero Tale, but when it comes to having a "best build", it's a whole different story. Since everyone can go for just about any nodes in the skill tree, I've created two Hero Tale builds to help you in the late game: a melee one and a ranged one. Following them in detail should help you in the end game immensely.

Just like in Path of Exile (if you've played it), you have a skill tree - or rather, a skill forest - with all sorts of different nodes that you can pick every time you level up. There are small nodes and major nodes, which give you additional effects when you take the nodes adjacent to them. Those are the ones you need to look out for.

For each of these two builds I made, I've written down a path on the skill tree that you could follow. And since the melee build is different from the ranged build, it goes without saying that you need a different weapon setup.

I've also added the equipment you can use for them, so whenever you reach the level where you can grind the area that drops said gear piece, then by all means, you should go farm there.

If you are completely new to the game, then you should first read the Hero Tale guide I created, where you can find a handful of tips and tricks to help you get started!

Feel free to check out the links below if you are interested in a particular build, and if you want to zoom in on the image, simply open it in a new tab or zoom in with your mobile device. Each image of the skill tree has a number corresponding to the order in which you should allocate these skills.

Oh, and nothing's set in stone! Like I said before, you can tweak each build and go for a specific node if you want, instead of the one I shared - it's just going to make the build slightly different! Ranged build  |  Melee build Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Let's start our Hero Tale best builds with the ranged build. Until recently, ranged builds had a significant advantage over melee builds. Because of that, they were very popular within the community. Even though that's not the case anymore, ranged builds didn't get any nerfs, or anything that would make them less potent.

So, here is a ranged build if you feel like giving it a try. Dark Skill Tree

This is the complete Dark tree, assuming that you have at least 11 points. If you only have 1 point, then just take the Ferocius Hunger node. Skill Tree

If this is your first run and you only have 1 Dark skill point, prioritize getting the critical chance and critical damage nodes first. After that, go for the health and defence nodes. Once you have all of them, get the movement speed ones. The last ones to take should be the magic nodes.

If you do have all of the dark skill nodes, take the HP nodes, then prioritize Hermes Feet and Hunter nodes. After that, you should move towards Falcon Agility.

Around level 50, take the HP nodes and keep going towards Man of Focus which increases your total power. Next is the Weak Spot Hunt node. Take all the little nodes until you get to the big one. This will increase your critical chance by a lot and, thus, your damage output.

You should be over level 60 now and it's time to start putting points toward Berserker Soul. Take all the little nodes until you get to the big one. These nodes will increase your critical multiplier. That's mainly why you want to get them after Weak Spot Hunt. Having a lot of critical strike multipliers without a high critical chance makes no sense.

Your skill tree at level 73 should look like this:

This set can be found at Barnaba's Shop at Deamon Market or as a reward for defeating Deamon Mercenary.

This bow can be purchased from the Inventor's Shop at the Inventor's Atelier. Until you get your final gear, always try to use the ones that give you the most damage output.

To give credit where it's due, this build was made by player @HabibTryHard. A simple guide can't possibly cover every boss fight featured in Hero Tale. If you want, you can check how the build performs on YouTube in a series that includes every single boss fight, from the beginning of the game to the end.

The developers reworked the block mechanic, and now melee builds are much more potent. Of course, you could play a melee build before, but it was not as good as it is now. It's just a lot easier after the update. So, if you want to try out a melee build in Hero Tale, check it out below! Dark Skill Tree

This is the full perks tree, assuming you have 12 points to allocate. If not, you should only take the node Ferocious Hunger. Skill Tree

This is the build's final skill tree at roughly level 188. In the early levels, you should prioritize taking the nodes Divine Immunity and Onrush.

Divine Immunity will boost your defence by 10%, and it also applies to stats you get from items.

Onrush lets you charge your attack while you are still searching for your next opponent. This can save you significant time when farming. After, you should start allocating points to your critical strike rate by taking Crit Master.

At around level 65, here's what your skill tree should look like:

This set can be found at Barnaba's Shop at Deamon Market or as a reward for defeating Deamon Mercenary.

This item can be found at Barnaba's Shop at Deamon Market.

It can be found as loot when you kill Monstrous Skeleton at the Graveyard. You might need to farm for this for some time.

You can get this sword as a loot by killing Necromancer in Shadow Temple. It's not the easiest drop to get, so be prepared for a long farming day.

This guide is based on a build created by @HabibTryHard, who has a great, detailed series that covers every boss fight from level 1 to level 188. Of course, I couldn't go into as much detail as they did, for obvious reasons. If you want to know something very specific or see how this build actually performs, you can take a look at their YouTube channel.

#4306. The Top 10 Best Horror Games To Play This Halloween

Humans are drawn to horror in all forms, real life and fiction. Perhaps it’s the desire to get as close to death as possible without actually dying; perhaps it’s the morality of life and knowing death comes for all of us; perhaps all our heads are just a little miswired. Whatever the reason, we flock to movies where supernatural entities and puppets on tricycles upend otherwise lovely lives, TV shows where murderous cults kill and stump local detectives, and books where the words on the page seem to follow you to bed. Games, however, go a step further, letting you enter the horror and control it (or become its victim), and you could argue that, as a result, they’re the most immersive form of fiction.

We at Game Informer love a healthy dose of horror from time to time, and we often review games like this. Some terrify us. Others… don’t. And the best ones stick with us for years and years after the credits. Below is a list of 10 of the best horror games we’ve played recently. This isn’t an all-time list, so don’t fret if your personal favorite isn’t here. Instead, this is a collection of 10 horror games ordered by release date that we think are great for spooky season and beyond. Let us know in the comments what you would add to the list!

The cozy corner of the horror genre seems to have exploded overnight, and now tons of new slice-of-life horror games are in various stages of development. That said, the team behind newcomer The Village in the Shade is no stranger to the form; they made the Yomawari series, a cute-and-terrifying collection of creepy virtual tales. The Village in the Shade takes things back to the homestead, giving you (a child who emerged from a hole in the ground and was immediately given the responsibility of running an entire farm by yourself) the freedom to plant, sow, reap, ranch, and more. Just follow the important rules: don't go out at night, don't share secrets, and don't leave the village among others. You wouldn't want to break the rules, right? You could, theoretically, go about your idyllic rural living. But as you unravel the threads of what this village is, who you are, and why you're here, it's hard not to get drawn into the strange, mysterious, delightfully disturbing truths hiding in its shadows. Just don't forget to water your turnips before you go sneaking out again.

Fans of survival horror and old-school FMV adventure games will find plenty to love (and fear) in Tenebris Somnia. When a young woman visits her ex-boyfriend’s apartment and discovers he's trapped in a hellish dream world, it kicks off a well-executed survival-horror trek of inventive puzzles and resource management to overcome dangerous monsters. High-production, live-action cutscenes help tell the story of a deteriorating relationship and the toll an indie horror film took on its creators, and they play an important role in gameplay. Tenebris Somnia may not look like much due to its classic pixelated presentation, but its scares and story captivate. – Our Review

Resident Evil Requiem is not just one of the best Resident Evil games, but it’s also one of the best horror games ever made. It features a unique dual-protagonist structure. Grace Ashcroft is timid, new to the whole “shooting zombies in the head while dealing with Umbrella viruses” thing, and is generally just trying to do her job. Leon S. Kennedy, however, is a veteran of all that and more. Requiem splits its runtime between the two characters, letting you experience both sides of Capcom’s marquee survival-horror style. Grace’s sections leave your hands clammy and your blood pressure high as you desperately try to survive. Leon’s sections leave your hands shaking with adrenaline and your blood pumping with excitement as he mows down zombies (sometimes literally, courtesy of those pesky chainsaws). The result is a Resident Evil game that blends two typical RE experiences – terrifying and tough or exhilarating over-the-top action – into one cohesive package. It’s perfect for someone who wants to feel scared and then soon after receive the catharsis of being the one in control, like being the tragic victim who dies in Act One of the horror movie and the last one standing who lives to tell the tale. – Our Review

Little Nightmares developer Tarsier Studios has a knack for delivering creepy side-scrolling adventures, but Reanimal eschews any whimsy to become its scariest game yet. While mechanically it is similar to Little Nightmares and still puts small children in unimaginable peril, Reanimal is capital-H horror thanks largely to its terrifying threats and disturbing animal-themed imagery (this probably isn’t the game for animal lovers; some messed-up stuff happens to these critters). Escaping the game’s island setting is thrilling and chilling whether you’re playing alone or with a friend in co-op. Months after release, we’re still thinking about Reanimal’s memorable final sequence, which is worth the price of admission on its own. – Our Review

2001’s Silent Hill 2 is considered one of the best horror video games of all time for good reason. At release, it was a graphical powerhouse, using the PlayStation 2's horsepower to create a setting that begged to be explored, even though every bone in your body said you shouldn’t. The remake from developer Bloober Team took on a big task in modernizing the game without losing the original’s soul, and it did a great job. Among all the recent Silent Hill releases (Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall), the remake is our favorite. The story of James Sunderland and his troubling relationship with his departed wife is complex, emotional, and – important for the purposes of this list – unsettling and scary. – Our Review

Alan Wake 2 is an excellent pick for some spooky madness, in the vein of David Lynch’s seminal Twin Peaks mystery-surrealist series. Don’t worry too much about the “2” part of the game’s title. You just need to know that the titular Alan Wake character is a not-great writer who acts like he’s really great, his wife is missing, and he got trapped in the ambiguous Dark Place. He’s only one half of the Alan Wake 2 equation, with his segments set in a dream-like version of New York City. Playing as him feels the most Twin Peaks-y. The other half is Saga, a police officer who arrives in the Pacific Northwest town of Bright Falls to investigate a murder that might be linked to a cult. You can expect more traditional survival-horror gameplay from her. But this is still a Remedy Entertainment game, and without spoiling anything, it goes places. And along the way, you can expect plenty of scares. Turn the lights down low (or off), light a candle, and sit back and enjoy one of Remedy’s best games. – Our Review

Square Enix has gone two-for-two with its Paranormasight series, an anthology of stories about the strange and occult. And while the more recent Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant tale all its own, the first entry – The Seven Mysteries of Honjo – brings significantly more scares. A group of people in the city of Honjo find themselves caught in a spectral battle royale, using powerful objects and conditions to curse one another, with the allure of a prize at the end. Its magic isn't just in the flowchart timeline, where you can hop between different perspectives and protagonists to see how events play out from every angle, but also in the gorgeous stereoscopic environments and narrative puzzles. Adventure games are a classic genre, and Paranormasight will remind you of what the genre is capable of the moment you slowly spin your camera around, your eyes peeking out from behind your fingers.

Survival horror can contain multitudes, and as the years have worn on, the genre has grown to encompass a wide range of action-combat mechanics. Signalis feels like a re-centering in that respect. It's an isometric survival-horror indie project from developer rose-engine, filled with clever puzzles, scarce resources, limited inventory slots, and looming, oppressive dread. As the Replika unit Elster, you delve deep into a remote complex filled with horrors and monsters, searching for something, or someone, waiting down below. While love for classic horror games and other hallmarks of genre fiction will certainly draw you in, the stylish presentation and devastatingly human core will keep you forging ahead to the finale. Once you've breached the surface of Signalis' retro-future super-structures, you won't be able to turn back.

In horror movies, audiences often groan at a protagonist for putting themselves in seemingly grave danger just to learn more about a cursed amulet or bloodthirsty killer. But in Immortality, you are the protagonist, and despite a lingering sense that you shouldn't be digging into the archives of these abandoned films, each eerie new scene makes you want to dive deeper. It's a game about Marisa Marcel, an actress who almost starred in three movies in the late 20th century, but has since disappeared. None of the movies were ever released due to mysterious circumstances, but you have access to the archived, unedited live-action footage, including behind-the-scenes conversations. By scrubbing through footage, you can select people or items in each scene and jump to random footage from any other movie that includes the same person or item. The approach to puzzle-solving is unique and keeps you appropriately disoriented. The mystery at the center is an unsettling treat to unravel, and scary in new and unexpected ways. Immortality is one of a kind and an easy recommendation for horror fans who want to try something a little different.

In the decade since launch, Dead by Daylight has continued to succeed, thanks to a dedicated (and newcomer-friendly) fanbase and its towering roster of original and licensed personas from across pop culture horror. The asymmetrical multiplayer title has become an anthology of horror’s biggest faces, including Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Pyramid Head, and even the Xenomorph. Whether you play as a Survivor, trying to escape all manner of nightmare locations through stealth and cunning, or as a Killer, whose experience feels more like a hunting club, you’ll understand why Dead by Daylight has become a recurring destination for fans of the gruesome and bizarre.

Read about the making of Dead by Daylight and how it sunk its teeth into millions of players in our six-page exclusive feature in Issue 368 (p. 42), available in our magazine archive to anyone with a free Game Informer account.

#4305. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

Android, PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, iOS

#4304. Every Pokémon Gimmick, Ranked

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Over the years, we have seen many different Pokémon gimmicks pop up. It seems like every generation of Pokémon needs to have its own gimmick to make it stand out from the others.

It has come to a point where many fans of the series are tired of seeing new gimmicks pop up, and they would rather Pokémon go back to its roots with simple turn-based battles.

Unfortunately, that is never going to be the case, so you must accept whatever gimmick is in each game. Some of these gimmicks aren’t bad, but other ones are rather questionable. Let’s compare each of these gimmicks and see how they stack up against each other.

After introducing Mega Evolutions to Pokémon, Game Freak needed something to top it. Unfortunately, the gimmick in the next games, Sun and Moon, ended up being what is considered the worst gimmick in the Pokémon series.

The gimmick in question is Z-Moves. Z-Moves allow your Pokémon to use a massively powerful move, provided they are holding the appropriate Z-Crystal. Many have said that requiring an item to use one all-powerful move is a bit lame.

These all-powerful moves are often viewed as the one-hit option, allowing you to clear battles easily without much strategy being involved. The gimmick often felt unbalanced, and the addition of annoying, unskippable cutscenes, made using the moves extremely annoying.

I am someone who absolutely loves the Paldea region. I think that it is a beautiful area, and the idea that battles are celebrated in massive arenas is actually really cool to me. However, this generation of Pokémon games has one of the worst gimmicks, and that is Dynamaxing.

Dynamaxing allows a Pokémon to grow massive, amplifying its power in the process, and giving it access to different moves. In theory, it sounds decent. However, it is a nightmare for competitive play, as it makes already extremely powerful Pokémon even more powerful instead of lifting up and helping weaker Pokémon.

In addition to this, the moves given to the Pokémon are not unique, as they become different moves based on the previous move’s type, so a flying-type move will always become the same move when Dynamaxed. There are even more issues with it, but it all boils down to the gimmick feeling like not much thought went into it, as it is rather unbalanced and makes battles a bit of a slog.

Our picks for the best Pokémon Champions teams that are sure to help you climb this season.

If you were around for the Ruby and Sapphire days of Pokémon, then you remember double battles. These changed the way that Pokémon battles were played, and then they were expanded on in a rather weird way when triple Battles and rotational Battles appeared in Pokémon Black and White.

These battle types have rarely appeared since their inception, and it is because they weren’t very popular at the time. Triple battles are simple, involving three Pokémon being on the field at once instead of two. This is a bit unnecessary, as double battles were already fine.

Additionally, rotational battles were annoying because you had the ability to rotate your Pokémon around whenever you wanted, making some moves completely obsolete. However, it did make things interesting because the mechanic of rotating your Pokémon was different from switching them in and out of battle.

Terastallization is a gimmick that has the fanbase rather mixed, as there are many who enjoy the mechanic, and then there are those who absolutely hate it. As far as things go, it is a rather middle-of-the-road gimmick that could have been better, but it isn’t that bad.

This gimmick, which was introduced in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, allows you to crystalize your Pokémon, changing its typing in the process. Many enjoy the mechanic because it lets you change the Pokémon’s typing, making them more resistant to moves they were once weak against.

The argument against Terastallization is that it can be unbalanced in certain battle formats, but it is mostly a balanced mechanic that works well with the series. The other argument is that every Pokémon looks absolutely terrible when it Terastalizes, and to be honest, they aren’t wrong.

Whether they're unlikely or just silly, these are the Ridiculous Pokémon Mega Evolutions We Would Love To See.

As stated earlier in the article, double battles were introduced in Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, and they have remained to this day. It is one of the few earlier gameplay gimmicks that people sometimes forget started as a gimmick because it was so beloved.

Never before had players thrown two Pokémon into battle at once, and it felt like a natural progression of the battle system, allowing players to have two Pokémon whose types complimented each other.

Plus, this generation introduced new moves that were meant to be used during double battles. This gimmick has not changed since its inception, and it is because it feels natural for the series. There is nothing that needs to be changed about it, which makes it one of the best Game Freak has added to the series.

Why is it that I always forget that Mega Evolution is something that started in Pokémon X and Y? I always think that it was the gimmick from Pokémon Black and White. Tangent aside, Mega Evolution has become the most popular gimmick that Game Freak has added to the games.

It is so popular that people have continuously asked for more and more Pokémon to receive Mega Evolutions because the transformations are not only cool, but they are meaningful.

When Mega Evolution happens, it can sometimes change a Pokémon’s type, it can change the Pokémon’s ability, and it boosts the Pokémon’s stats tremendously. This can change the tide of a battle, but it isn’t so powerful that it is the ultimate trump card. It doesn’t allow you to blow away the opposition, but rather gives you more of a fighting chance and can dramatically help in certain situations. To this day, there are still Mega Evolutions being created, and it has been the focus in some competitive games as well.

I've missed Pokemon's Mega Evolution mechanic, and it's going to be a huge draw for Pokemon Legends: Z-A players.

#4303. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 to reach first Worlds semi-final since 2019

Invictus Gaming knocked out fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening quarter-final of Worlds 2026 in Allen, Texas. The result guarantees China a semi-final place after the LPL's 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage.

Invictus Gaming are through to the last four of Worlds 2026. They beat fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening match of the Knockout Stage. The series was played at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas, on 3 November (US time).

The win guarantees China a semi-final place. That matters after the LPL’s 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage. IG now meet either Gen.G or LYON. Gen.G beat IG 1-0 in the Swiss Stage and finished it with a perfect 3-0 record.

TES played the event without ZUIAN. On 6 October the club announced that Bai ‘369’ Jia-Hao would move into the starting line-up because of visa problems affecting ZUIAN.

The stand-in still made his mark. IG won Game 1 after building a gold lead of more than 10,000. TES levelled in Game 2 when 369, on Renekton, killed JiaQi and TheShy on his own late in the game. IG then took the next two games to close out the series.

Every Knockout Stage match is a single-elimination best-of-five played with Fearless Draft. The two sides knew each other well. They met twice in best-of-five series in September. IG won 3-2 in the LPL Split 3 playoffs on 5 September. TES won 3-1 in the LPL Regional Finals on 17 September.

The prize money gap is now fixed. Worlds 2026 has a total prize pool of US$5,000,000, with US$1,000,000 for the winner. Each losing semi-finalist receives US$400,000, so IG are guaranteed at least that sum.

IG’s run began with a mid-season rescue. The team started LPL Split 3 in the Nirvana Group. The club then asked TheShy and Rookie, who were both on a break, to come back. The pair helped the side qualify for Worlds. Both won the 2018 world title with IG.

TheShy said he had promised IG’s CEO he would help if asked. “I came back to keep my word,” he said after the series.

The #Worlds2026 Knockout Stage bracket after today's match! pic.twitter.com/iaPQndNZSW

— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 4, 2026

The rest of the quarter-finals follow this week. Gen.G play LYON on 4 November. Dplus KIA face Bilibili Gaming on 5 November. Europe’s last team, Karmine Corp, play T1 on 6 November. All three start at 16:00 CT.

The semi-finals will be played in Allen on 7 and 8 November. The final will be held in Brooklyn on Saturday 14 November at 2pm EST.
