All have been tried and tested, some were a hit and others a complete miss, but in the end, the definitive list is here, and it's actually quite fun! A little backstory I will start by mentioning this: from the very beginning, I didn't know what to expect. I went in blind, I made mistakes, but didn't think too much of it. Those mistakes later translated into death (of my character, of course), so I tried again, and again, and again.

Eventually, I figured it out, which is why it wasn't exactly easy to create a guide that encapsulates everything.

My goal is to give clear directions for each build, as well as a complete build for beginners to help you out in the early stages.

Free classes vs premium classes As you're probably well aware by now, there are 2 free classes you can pick, while the rest you'll have to pay for - they're premium. I believe you don't have to pay for the classes to actually enjoy the whole thing, but if you want to get them, that's perfectly fine too.

This can be enjoyed as F2P, which is why I've also covered builds for those free classes too. Oh and if you like the genre, we have a list of games like Vampire Survivors, which you might be interested in! They're based on my experience - I tested a lot of equipment, abilities and blessings, and this article has what I consider to be the best ones. New player build

As a new player, you won't have the gear required to follow any specific build. So, I figured it would be nice to also add a build that can serve as a guideline. This "generic" build will help you progress and clear content until you get gear, unlock characters, and can focus on something specific. Starting out The first gear you should get is the Plated Boots and Plated Armor. These can be a very solid foundation for any build you want to follow.

Since you won't have any blessings or stats from the compendium, I'll use the Exterminator class as an early-game example to give you an idea as to how to build pretty much any character in the early stages. Stats Priority Early on, you won't have any potions to reroll or lock any stats, so there's a lot of RNG involved. Focus on scaling one offensive option - in this case, we are going for burn damage, and then focus on survivability.

If you have Plated Boots and Armor, you already have a decent base block, so it makes sense to try and max that stat.

Dragon's Breath burn will be your main source of damage. Don't be surprised if you see more than 10-12 million damage just from the burn alone at the end of your run.

Make sure to use the well to send any items to your stash so you can eventually follow a more specific build.

This build focuses on attack speed, high damage, and area of effect (AoE). The core item of this build is Wind Crown, a helmet that gives ATK Speed based on the charges you have (up to +50%).

For the rings, I like to use Guiding Star for the extra attack/move speed, paired with Echoing Band. As an alternative, you can go with Copper Ring and Wooden Ring. Equipment Headwear Wind Crown Necklace Collar of Confidence Armor Blood-Soaked Shirt Gloves Quickhand Gloves Boots Spike Boots / Berserker Boots Rings Guiding Star / Echoing Band / Copper Ring / Wooden Ring Mark Mark of the Sword

Abilities Since this build is scaling AoE, it makes sense to prioritise abilities that benefit from it.

Stats Priority Obviously, there's a lot of RNG, and sometimes not even all the flasks in the world can save you, but anyway, here's what you should be looking for.

Blessings / Compendium At this point, it should be very obvious what you are looking for, but regardless, here we go.

Archer is a class known for its high attack speed, critical, and critical bonus chances. This is a build with these things in mind. The goal is to move around the map fast while dealing a lot of projectile damage to clear hordes of enemies. Equipment Headwear Wind Crown Necklace Blood Catcher Armor Blood-Soaked Shirt Gloves Quickhand Gloves Boots Running Shoes / Berserker Boots Rings Guiding Star / Echoing Band / Copper Ring / Wooden Ring Mark Mark of the Arrow / Mark of the Sword

Abilities In order of priority, you want to go with the following abilities:

Stats Priority With this build, you want to move fast so you can kite the mobs, deal critical damage, and sustain with Blood Cather and Blood-Soaked Shirt.

This Exterminator build is all about stacking burn with Flame Crown + Ring of Fire + Flame Strike. Stack Area and Burn Chance early, and you’ll melt hordes before they even reach you. Equipment Headwear Flame Crown Necklace Collar of Confidence Armor Blazing Shell Gloves Sparking Tips Boots Firewalker Boots Rings Ring of Fire / Echoing Band / Seal of Rebirth Mark Mark of the Flame / Mark of the Arrow

Abilities Flame Strike is a must, obviously. Astronomer's Orb is pretty good considering this is a mid-range build, plus we are scaling move speed and range. Lightning Strikes for AoE clear and spark/burn.

Stats Priority Any of these stats is good to prioritise, but burn change + damage are better during the early levels.

Blessings / Compendium Since this isn't a crit build for a change, this is how the blessings look:

The Cleric build relies on AoE scaling, piercing, and ATK Speed. For this build, you don't care about crit. Your goal is to get the Wind Crown helm, and stack it with Radiant Aura. Essentially, you will focus on getting more damage and tankiness, and you're good. Equipment Headwear Wind Crown Necklace Collar of Confidence / Jade Amulet Armor Hunter’s Garb / Blood-Soaked Shirt Gloves Quickhand Gloves / Hunting Gloves Boots Spike Boots / Electrostatic Treads Rings Guiding Star / Seal of Rebirth Mark Mark of the Cleric

Abilities Radiant Aura works best with the Cleric, in my experience.

Stats Priority ATK Speed and Damage go hand in hand for the Cleric. The Area is a must for the Aura too.

Blessings / Compendium As you can see, Revive is for the Cleric something you should get, just like you would for any other class. In terms of other blessings, anything that works to boost the stats of the abilities is welcome.

#4299. The Legend of Neverland best class

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version 1.0.65

As in most other video games, The Legend of Neverland classes are not perfectly balanced. And to be strong, you need to not only play the game correctly but use a good class as well. Read on, and you will learn what the best class in The Legend of Neverland is. WHAT IS THE BEST CLASS IN THE LEGEND OF NEVERLAND?

The first thing you need to know is there are 6 classes in The Legend of Neverland: Warrior, Ranger, Craftsman, Lancer, Ninja and Scholar. As you'd expect, each class is designed for a different playstyle.

Each of these classes can be played in two different ways, each one of these specialising in something - for instance, if you take the Warrior class, it can either spec into a Berserker or a Gladiator. The Berserker is the class that focuses on DPS, while the Gladiator is the tank.

So, when talking about the most powerful class in The Legend of Neverland, everything depends on your preferences and in-game experience. For example, it's best to use the Marksman Ranger if you are a skilled player, rather than a beginner. They can deal excellent damage and be the main DPS in most battles.

However, if you are a beginner, the best choice is something that is inherently strong, doesn't rely 100% on combos and positioning, and lets you take your time to learn the role. One such choice could be the Gladiator Warrior. Gladiators have the highest HP, so you can make more mistakes without being punished as much.

On the following pages, I shared a little bit more info about each individual class, so make sure you go and check them out if you're eager! Warrior  |  Ranger  |  Scholar Lancer  |  Craftsman  |  Ninja

The Warrior is a melee class that is typically associated with "fighters". This class has two sub-classes, Gladiator and Berserker, each one following a completely different path and ranking at each end of the tier list.

The playstyle is fairly easy regardless of which one you pick, and it is a pretty beginner-friendly class if I could even say that. You have balanced stats, decent survivability, damage, but it tends to be a little bit boring from a playstyle point of view. At least, to me. Gladiator

This is an extremely good class end-game, in both PvE and PvP, and I strongly recommend you choose it if you like the Warrior class. The Gladiator has good damage (for a tank at least), an insanely good kit for PvP, and it is fun to see players struggling to kill you. Of course, I'm talking end-game, when your character is maxed out.

It is a good class for those who don't like to rely on anyone or anything. Berserker

As much as I would have loved to have the Berserker top-tier, once you start playing it, you just feel that it is missing something. It has damage, it is flexible, but to me it doesn't cut it. He is not nearly as good as the Gladiator, and despite having okay-ish damage, it does die fairly easily.

The Ranger is a reliable class, one that is fun to play (if you like ranged classes, that is) and whose damage is good, well into the end-game. They can be more support-oriented or damage-oriented, and depending on which one of the two you pick, you can't go wrong.

When it comes to the Ranger playstyle, it is not as beginner-friendly as other classes. You always need to be mindful about your positioning, and make sure you don't get one-shot by enemies. This class is fairly squishy by default, even though the Windchaser is slightly more tanky than the Marksman. I'd still suggest you avoid damage. Marksman

Even though the Marksman is a full damage class, it is not flexible, has no survivability, and no support whatsoever. It is a glass cannon. I am not a fan of this class personally, unless you are a master at positioning and have good reflexes. Still, even then, some players find it hard to play it. I am one of those players. Windchaser

If you want to play a ranged class that can be good at everything, the Windchaser is a very good pick. You should always consider their supportive skills, since in PvP those will come in handy. They'll also be pretty good for dungeons/instances, so try to pick equipment that enhances that, instead of damage.

We're finally covering the class I absolutely adore. The Scholar is the basic class I started this game with, and then I specialised in becoming a Priest. Don't take that literally, just the class, I mean - the healer. I like the fact that good Scholars are needed in virtually every instance, they have a good time on the battlefield focusing on buffs and debuffs, and they can survive fairly well.

All you need to do is avoid damage, and deal with whatever opponents you can. The roles of the Scholar can also be that of a DPS, but it's a fairly difficult one to master. Judge

The Judge is the equivalent of a "mage". This class can deal good damage, they can offer some support, and honestly speaking, if you ever face a Judge who knows exactly how to combo and survive, you'll be obliterated and in awe. It does require some practice to figure everything out though, so it's not for those who want a casual playstyle, where they just go with the flow. Priest

This is the one class I cannot praise enough. The Priest is amazing for every single content, and they are, in fact, required for most teams. They offer heals, buffs, debuffs, and ell that you can imagine. They're honestly a menace to deal with, so if you like being a support main, you should pick Priest.

Playing as a Lancer is always fun. You have some range, you have some melee, and you have a TRUCKLOAD of damage, regardless of what you pick. Ever since this class got released, they are constantly in the top tier, and I can tell you exactly why.

The Lancer is a very intuitive class, it's pretty easy to learn, and it is good. If you want a single class that can be good, reliable and fun, Lancer is the answer. Dragon Knight

As a Dragon Knight, you have slightly less damage than a Dragon Fighter, but a lot more survivability. Both of the classes I consider to be equally good, it's just about finding the one that you like the most in terms of gameplay. Dragon Fighter

If I was to pick between the two, I think Dragon Fighter would be one of my favourites. It does extremely good damage, it has sustain, it's easy to understand, and if you just hit the right skills, everyone is going to think you're a pro. It's fun!

As a Craftsman, you rely a lot on your creations. It's a class that is fun to play, but is not that amazing in PvP. It's good if you like mechanical stuff and only want to go do bosses and general PvE content. Armorer

The Armorer is not a great class, unless you want to do PvE and bosses. You can do amazingly, even God-tier for PvE, but when it comes to PvP, the lack of survivability makes them one-shot. Mechanician

This class is not that great for either PvE or PvP, and until someone figures some better use for it, it's quite a pity.

The Ninja is the latest class in The Legend of Neverland, and it is a class that is close-ranged, but deadly. It is fun to play, but not easy. I would argue they can be good for PvP, but they need some support when it comes to PvE. Blazing Owl

Blazing Owl is good, it has a very solid kit for both PvP and PvE. I am not personally a fan of the playstyle, but if you like assassin-like characters, this is a good one. You can be good once you learn the skills in both PvE and PvP, and you can always go finish off enemies that have low HP. Shadow Owl

Shadow Owl is similar to Blazing Owl in a way, and their play styles are not all that different. They both rely on an assassin-like approach, but Shadow Owl is a lot more fun - especially in PvE. In PvP it could be too, but it is situational (depends on the enemies you're facing). Both of the classes are going to take some time getting used to.

CONCLUSION If you are a beginner, the best class to opt for is the Gladiator. And if you are a more experienced player, the best option is the Ranger. It will allow you to deal more damage and play a central role during the battle. And while you are here, take a look at our The Legend of Neverland codes list for some free goodies.

#4298. Gen.G sweep LYON to end North America’s Worlds 2026 run and set up iG semi-final

Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.

#4297. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4293. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

As part of a free update, The Sims 4 has kicked off a new collaboration with Coach, which means there's free stuff for everyone.

The Sims 4’s first update of the year is here, though it may not be quite what you might have expected. The game’s latest patch mainly centres around a collaboration with Coach, the luxury fashion brand.

This obviously isn’t the game’s first collaboration with a known brand, though this one does include a lot of free items and accessories that anyone can make use of, even if they don’t care about Coach.

The Coach Collection brings nine new items to The Sims 4. They range from clothes and accessories you can use with Create a Sim, to decoration items available in Build Buy. There’s also The Carriage House, a new Gallery household where you can find three new roommates.

There’s a nice bit of variety in the options available, some casual and others more practical for your Sims to wear. Then there’s The Bag Room, which can also be grabbed from the Gallery. The room simply serves as a way for you to show off your Coach bags and trunks collection.

In case you missed it, The Sims’ development team recently shared an update on some of what we can expect in 2026, both for The Sims 4 as well as other projects currently in the works. It even included further confirmation, if any was needed, that Project Rene is a dedicated mobile off-shoot, and not — as many had long believed — The Sims 5.

#4288. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4286. Shigeru Miyamoto Proclaims November 1 is Pikmin Day, Pikmin 4 Demo Coming To Switch 2 Soon

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

Aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

The Switch 2 version of the game (you can read Game Informer’s Pikmin 4 review here) will have improved visuals and take advantage of the Switch 2’s mic to let you say things like “Rush” and “Go to work” to Oatchi. The Dandori Academy side of the game is essentially time trials you can practice, and then on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, you will have one chance to post your best time. You can read more about the Switch 2 version of the game here.

Miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial update soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

The Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

Finally, Miyamoto brought actress Fuka Koshiba on the presentation (best known for voicing Kiki in Kiki’s Delivery Service) to share her appreciation for the Pikmin franchise (she likes to knit Pikmin hats that she shares on social media) and introduce a Pikmin short film. In the short, a Pikmin interacts with a toad, but I won’t spoil what happens. Miyamoto promised more shorts are on the way and in the future, they will be found in the Nintendo Today app.

Unfortunately, the stream concluded without a single reference to 2017's Hey! Pikmin. I wouldn't expect it to get a port to Switch 2 anytime soon.

EA Sports has revealed the much-anticipated Ultimate Team of the Year cards for the 2025/26 season, including a slew of meta favourites from the likes of the evergreen Virgil van Dijk, super-fast Kylian Mbappe and unplayable queen of FC 26 Claudia Pina.

Elsewhere Lionesses Alessia Russo, Lucy Bronze and Leah Williamson feature alongside now-obligatory Barcelona duo Alexia Putellas and Aitana Bonmati. However, the Team of the Year selection hasn’t been without controversy. The FC 26 TOTY promo is voted for by players, you probably cast your vote by selecting time-limited gold cards yourself, but that method has led some to question whether the Team of the Year is more of a popularity contest than a true measure of performance. This is with specific reference to Virgil, whose in-and-out form during Liverpool’s poor start this season has caused some to question his eight-straight inclusion.

In yet another blow to those of us who got Mario Gomez and Gianluca Vialli from the Classic XI Hero pack, during the TOTY event these Classic XI Heroes will be further upgraded to TOTY Honorable Mentions Heroes.

More TOTY items will also be dropping over the next couple of weeks, including a men’s and women’s 12th player, Honorable Mentions, 2 teams of TOTY Icons and both a men’s and women’s “Captain of the Year”.

#4284. The MongolZ end FURIA’s winning run as NAVI send Falcons out of IEM Beijing

The MongolZ beat world No.1 FURIA to reach the IEM Beijing semi-finals, while NAVI eliminated big-spending Falcons in the group stage. The results reshape the picture of the main contenders before the PGL Major Singapore opens on 24 November.

Against world No.1 FURIA on Wednesday, The MongolZ recovered after dropping the opening map. MOUZ have also booked a semi-final place after going unbeaten in Group B.

The defeat ended a seven-game winning run for FURIA, HLTV said, although the match was not an elimination game. FURIA had not lost since winning PGL Masters Bucharest. They now face BetBoom in the quarter-finals.

The second map, Cache, was FURIA’s own pick, and The MongolZ had lost on that map in each of their previous four attempts. This time they won it, then closed out the series on the third map.

The timing gives the result extra weight. IEM Beijing is ESL’s top-tier CS2 event and the last big tournament before the Major. FURIA are still alive, but the series shows they can be beaten by the sides around them.

Falcons went out in the Group A lower-bracket final. NAVI recovered from a narrow loss on the opening map and dominated the rest of the series. On the Mirage decider, NAVI won all 12 rounds of their T-side half.

w0nderful went 25-4 on Inferno. b1t then took over on Mirage.

For a big-spending organisation, an exit before the playoffs is a setback. Falcons share seventh to eighth place with Team Liquid, and the two teams earn the same amount. That compares with $360,000 for the champions.

Liquid also fell at the final hurdle. BetBoom beat them 2-1 to take the last playoff place in Group B. A zorte ace in round 23 of the Mirage decider swung the series. PARIVISION, who finished behind MOUZ in Group B, meet NAVI in the other quarter-final.

The $1,250,000 prize pool is split into $300,000 in player prize money and $950,000 in club share. The event is being played at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena in Beijing. It is listed as an ESL Pro Tour Masters event.

The playoffs are single-elimination best-of-three series. A best-of-three third-place match will also be played, and the grand final is best-of-five.

🏟️ Bloomage Biotech·Biohyalux ECM Arena pic.twitter.com/pr3rqLDijc

— ESL Counter-Strike (@ESLCS) November 4, 2026

Both quarter-finals take place on Friday 6 November, at 14:30 and 17:45 local time. The semi-finals follow on Saturday 7 November. The grand final is on Sunday 8 November.

Attention then turns to the PGL Major Singapore, the second CS2 Major of 2026. Its last four days will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, which holds more than 12,000 spectators.
